title: Configurable NoC IP: safety verification and tool integration
summary: Historical safety verification models, generated bindings, register enumeration and later configuration-tool release setup.

dates.note: Null boundaries preserve unknown project/rotation dates. Inspected author/committer milestones are identified in evidence; they are not employment, project-start, shipment or acceptance dates.

facts.text: Worked in a configurable SystemVerilog interconnect environment combining Python parameter generation, generated testbench bindings, UVM/VIP simulation and fault-site tooling.

The local NoC repository review covers 22 Michael-authored objects across all 2,316 local refs: 20 ordinary commits (13 in selected HEAD, seven on other histories), plus a stash and empty index snapshot; ordinary commits have 17 distinct stable patch identities.

Inspected ordinary author dates cluster in November 2020–April 2021 and December 2024. The August 2026 objects are stashed debugging state, not evidence of a later landed feature or continuous NoC project tenure.
Supported configuration-tool integration with NoC end-to-end validation by updating tool-module selections on multiple release histories and correcting a malformed version value.

A five-file 2026 stash contains absent-route guards, credit-aware OWO target derivation and numeric clock-frequency comparisons; it is retained only as private debugging context, with no landed-change or passing-test claim.

Michael authored selected validation models, generated-binding changes and register-enumeration refactoring. The NoC IP, initial fault-injection framework, later ECC correction, read beat-counter monitor and FMU integration remain collaborative or other-author work.

Legacy model files survive at the captured HEAD, but their top-level instances and legacy interrupt aggregation were removed in a colleague’s 2022 change; retained source and blame do not prove current execution or active top-level use.

notes: 2026-10-29 read-only local Git/source research establishes attributable historical implementation, not new owner confirmation, fresh employer test execution, sole IP ownership or functional-safety certification.
